Bloomfield Municipal Court is a city courthouse in Bloomfield, New Mexico. It’s the 16th largest court in New Jersey State and the 3rd largest in the county of Essex. The court's core value is to provide fairness, independence, integrity, and quality service to the Bloomfield people. It has jurisdiction over non-criminal cases involving Village and Town Ordinance violations in the form of traffic citations and Municipal Code violations. All issues for hearing in this court are violations within the town and village limits.

How to find records?

Bloomfield Municipal Court records can be found online in the following ways:

  • Searching by name
  • Searching by case number
  • Searching by address
  • Searching by phone
  • Searching by email

Some recorded information is confidential and is not found online. For these types of records, a person had to submit an open record request to the clerk's office. Download and fill in all the information on the form and send it to the court clerk's office. The court will then decide whether to provide you with that record information or not.

What are the duties and roles of a clerk?

Bloomfield Municipal Court Clerk's role is to help the judges to perform their duties. The clerk's office also contains certificates, passports, copies, and permits; a person had to submit the documents at their office for further case proceedings or papers. They also solve queries, collect fines and help the judge outside the court. The clerk's office is an agent of licensing and custodians of the town records. It acts as the governing body secretary that makes agendas for the meetings and as the municipality's chief registrar of voters.

How would a person file a complaint in court?

A person can file a complaint in court by reading all the instructions provided by the court on the website in the form of how to file a citizen complaint. The person against which the complaint is filed must be 18+, and the incident must take place in the court town. After you file the complaint, the next step is that the judge will see the complaint and determine whether that incident is actual and whether the person against whom the complaint is filed is the one who committed the incident or not. After this, the municipal prosecutor will handle the case until it is solved.

How to make payments?

Bloomfield Municipal Court pay tickets can be made in the following ways:

In-Person

A person can make payment by visiting the court during business hours and paying in cash, checks, or with a card at the violation counter. Service or deduction charges of 2.99% will be applied if you pay with a credit card.

Online

A person can pay online using the New Jersey Municipal Court Direct Website https://www.bloomfieldtwpnj.com/438/NJMCDirect.com. Processing fees will be applied in this method.

Mail

A Person can send a certified check or money order to the court's mailing address. The address is 1 Municipal Plaza, 2nd Floor-LEB Room 227, and Bloomfield, NJ 07003. Do not send cash or personal checks in the mail; only certified checks are accepted.

Which forms are available by this court?

Bloomfield Municipal Court Forms that are available by this court are:

  • Forms for a public defender
  • Forms for record request
  • Forms for appeal packets
  • Citizen complaints
  • Forms for court request data

What is the amount of fines given on violation by the court?

Bloomfield Municipal Court Fine money depends upon the violation a person had done. For example, the fine for parking in a fire lane is $30, the penalty for the U-turn prohibited is $100, the fine for parking in the permit only is $50, the fine for using an abandoned vehicle is $30, and the penalty for overtime meter or meter feeding is $35.

How to get a marriage license?

Bloomfield Municipal Court marriage license is obtained from the clerk's office. The fee for a marriage license is $40 and for certificates is $20 per copy. The couple's age must be 18+. The couple must be presented in court when they come for the license. To obtain the permit, the couple had to submit a marriage form with a birth certificate, photo ID like a driver’s license, passport, or anything that could prove their identity. If anyone is divorced, a divorce paper must be submitted before getting support. If anyone wants the copies, fill out the certificated copy of the marriage license request, send the social security number and submit it to the court. The license is valid for up to 65 days, and a marriage ceremony is held in court after receiving it.

What are the rights of a person as a public defender in this court?

The right of a person as a public defender in the Bloomfield Municipal court are:

  • The court must inform the charges against you; it is your right to know about them.
  • Retain an attorney is your right
  • You have the right to appeal for conviction within 20 days
  • To testify on your behalf, you have the right to call or subpoena a witness

FAQ:

What is the court code?

Bloomfield municipal court code is 0702.

Which union provides the certified copy for the marriage license?

Civil union provides the certified copy for a marriage license.

What happens if I do not pay the fine on time?

If you do not pay a fine or speeding ticket on time, an extra penalty will be added, your license or insurance will be canceled, and sometimes warrants will be issued against you.

What If I plead guilty or am found guilty and don’t have the funds to pay the fine?

If you do not have funds to pay for the fine, then you can fill out a financial questionnaire, and then the judge will see if you are eligible for financial aid or not.

What are the etiquettes for the courtroom?

Bloomfield Municipal Court etiquettes are:

  • No electronic or food items are allowed in the court. Cell phones should be switched off.
  • During court proceedings, no recording or speaking is allowed· County Tax annually certificate
  • Weapons are not allowed in the courtroom
  • Wear suitable, respectable and comfortable clothes. Take off your hats, caps, or sunglasses after entering the courtroom
  • Only those children are allowed in the court that is a part of the case
